review_output.summary: The new async-search logging tests call `mockLog.assertAllExpectationsMatched()` right after submitting with `wait_for_completion_timeout=0ms`, so the check races with shard execution.
review_output.failure_scenario: Submit returns before the data-node shards fail, so no debug log has been emitted yet. The seen-expectation tests (Default/False) then fail intermittently because the latch has not counted down. The unseen-expectation test (True) passes even if logging is broken, because nothing has been logged yet. The submit-and-poll loop before the mockLog block runs a separate search outside the capture, so it does not help. Use `awaitAllExpectationsMatched()` or poll the search started inside the capture block until it finishes.

review_output.summary: `createClusterService(threadPool)` returns a started ClusterService that is never closed, in both `testMaybeWrapListenerForStackTrace` and `testMaybeWrapListenerForStackTraceLogs`.
review_output.failure_scenario: `ClusterServiceUtils.createClusterService` calls `clusterService.start()`, which starts the applier and master services and their executors. Nothing calls `close()`, so the threads and resources leak and the randomized-testing thread-leak checker can fail the suite. Wrap the service in try-with-resources, or use a mocked ClusterService or DiscoveryNode instead.

review_output.summary: The scroll `executeQueryPhase` now uses the stored legacy context's original channel version instead of the scroll request's own transport channel version (`channel.getVersion()`).
review_output.failure_scenario: In a mixed-version cluster, a scroll created through a new coordinator and continued through an old coordinator (older than ERROR_TRACE_IN_TRANSPORT_HEADER) passes the version check. The `error_trace` header is then missing, so it is read as false and stack traces are stripped for a node that never opted in. The reverse case also happens. Before this change the per-request channel version was used.

review_output.summary: In rank-feature and QuerySearchRequest, the version check now uses `readerContext.getShardSearchRequest(...)` rather than the incoming request's own channel version.
review_output.failure_scenario: For a LegacyReaderContext, `getShardSearchRequest` ignores its argument and returns the stored request. So the error-trace version check, and the debug log's shard id, come from the original request rather than from the rank-feature or query request on the current channel. Header handling can then be wrong when the current hop came from a node with a different version.

review_output.summary: `Configurator.setLevel("org.elasticsearch.search.SearchService", DEBUG)` in `@BeforeClass` is never reset. The same happens in AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT and inside `SearchServiceTests.testMaybeWrapListenerForStackTraceLogs`.
review_output.failure_scenario: Other suites in the same JVM inherit DEBUG logging for SearchService, so logs get noisy and log-level-dependent assertions can behave differently depending on test order. The existing `@TestLogging(value="org.elasticsearch.search.SearchService:DEBUG", reason=...)` annotation sets and restores the level automatically.

review_output.summary: `event.getThrown().getMessage().equals(exceptionMessage)` throws an NPE when the logged throwable has a null message.
review_output.failure_scenario: Any DEBUG event on the matched logger whose exception has a null message (for example `new RuntimeException()` or an NPE) throws inside the appender's `match()`. That breaks log capture or surfaces as a confusing error instead of a non-match. Use `Objects.equals(exceptionMessage, thrown.getMessage())`.

review_output.summary: `PatternAndExceptionSeenEventExpectation` duplicates the regex matching in the existing `PatternSeenEventExpectation` and inherits unused `message` matching state from SeenEventExpectation.
review_output.failure_scenario: Two near-identical pattern matchers now have to be maintained, and the nested `if (exceptionMatches) { if (patternMatches) ... }` could be a single condition. Extend or compose `PatternSeenEventExpectation` with an exception predicate instead.

review_output.summary: `addUnseenLoggingExpectations` adds one expectation for every node and shard pair, each with an exact message, when one wildcard expectation would cover them all.
review_output.failure_scenario: This creates nodes × shards expectations that each scan every log event. Any change to the message format (for example the node-id prefix) silently makes all of them vacuous. A single `UnseenEventExpectation` using `"*Clearing stack trace before transport:*"` covers all nodes and shards.

review_output.summary: Six new tests copy the same request-building code (JSON body, msearch NByteArrayEntity setup, and the mockLog try block), changing only the `error_trace` value and seen/unseen choice.
review_output.failure_scenario: The same pattern is repeated again in AsyncSearchErrorTraceIT, so fixing the query or the assertion means editing many copies. A helper that takes the `error_trace` parameter (null/true/false) and the expectation type would replace them.

review_output.summary: Every shard failure is logged with its full stack trace at DEBUG, including routine failures like cancellations and missing contexts, and the message has no request context beyond the shard.
review_output.failure_scenario: When SearchService DEBUG is turned on to diagnose a failure, task cancellations and search-context-missing failures across many shards each produce a full stack trace, which buries the useful entries. Filtering on `ExceptionsHelper.status(e)` or the exception type before logging would avoid flooding the log.
